authority: P0_IMPLEMENTATION_SPEC.md 8.3 (uncertainty is recorded, never assumed away)
P0_IMPLEMENTATION_SPEC.md 8.4 (dedup scope: suppression at L1/L2/L4; opportunities included)
artifact.note: This artifact is the identity authority. No host rule, tracking parameter, legal suffix, ATS pattern, outcome name or reason code is hardcoded in Python; every one of them is read from here, so an auditor can answer 'why did the system consider these two postings the same job?' without reading code.
not_authority_for: Eligibility. Identity is not a policy layer and never produces or alters a gate verdict (P0_SPEC 2.3).
Application state. Identity never reads or writes status, stage, scores or human decisions.
Compensation and work mode. Those belong to policy/jobops-policy-0.1.0.json.

layers.description: Source-native posting id, namespaced by portal. LinkedIn job ids are numeric and stable.
Canonicalized posting URL: scheme and host normalized, tracking parameters stripped, fragment removed, listing and root URLs rejected as identities.

layers.suppression_note: P0_SPEC 8.4 grants suppression at L1/L2/L4 confidence only. An exact L3 match is therefore a probable duplicate for human review, never a definite one.
layers.description: Conservative composite. Exact equality of all three normalized components. No token reordering, no synonym expansion, no geographic inference, no similarity scoring.
Employer ATS requisition id, namespaced by ATS system and tenant. A bare requisition id is never an identity on its own: the same number is issued independently by unrelated ATS systems.

definite_duplicate.name: DEFINITE_DUPLICATE
definite_duplicate.condition: Matched at a suppression-grade layer (L1, L2 or L4) with no contradiction at another high-confidence layer.

probable_duplicate.name: PROBABLE_DUPLICATE
probable_duplicate.condition: Matched exactly at L3 only. P0_SPEC 8.4 does not grant L3 suppression grade, so identity is not asserted and the candidate is linked to its probable match and surfaced.

identity_uncertain.name: IDENTITY_UNCERTAIN
identity_uncertain.condition: A near-match rather than an exact match (P0_SPEC 8.3), or a match at one high-confidence layer contradicted by another. Retained, linked to its probable match, surfaced to the human. Never auto-merged.

distinct.name: DISTINCT
distinct.condition: No layer matched and no near-match was produced.

pair_outcome_rule: Within one candidate/record pair the outcome is decided by the strongest layer that matched, then downgraded to IDENTITY_UNCERTAIN if any conflict rule fires for that same pair. A conflict never upgrades an outcome.
overall_outcome_precedence_note: Across pairs, the candidate's outcome is that of its strongest pair. A clean L1 match against one record is not weakened by a near-match against a different record - identity with the first record is established evidence, and the near-match is retained in matches[] and reported as has_uncertain_match rather than discarded or allowed to mask the established match.

url_canonicalization.strip_fragment_note: P0_SPEC 8.2: a listing-page URL with a #fragment 'is not a posting'. The fragment is removed, and a URL that has nothing but a root path once the fragment is gone is rejected as an identity rather than stored as one.
url_canonicalization.strip_leading_www_note: www is the only subdomain stripped for undeclared hosts. Blanket subdomain stripping is unsafe: for a Workday tenant host the subdomain IS the employer, and for jobs.lever.co it is the product.
url_canonicalization.lowercase_path_note: Paths are case-sensitive on many hosts. Two paths differing only in case are treated as different identities rather than silently merged.
url_canonicalization.tracking_parameters_note: Matched case-insensitively. Unrecognized parameters are KEPT: a parameter such as ?id=NIM2919 carries the posting identity, and dropping unknown parameters would silently merge distinct postings.
url_canonicalization.bare_listing_paths_note: Applied only when the URL carries no query string. https://site.com/job?id=NIM2919 is a posting; https://site.com/jobs is a listing.

host_families.name: linkedin
host_families.note: in.linkedin.com/jobs/view/<slug>-<id> and www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/<id> are the same posting because the same source-native id is present in both paths. The canonical form is rebuilt from that id, so the slug is not treated as identity-bearing.

host_families.name: lever
host_families.note: A single-segment path such as /Sprinto is a company board, not a posting, and is rejected as an identity.

host_families.name: workday
host_families.note: The tenant is the leading host label and is preserved. The host is not rewritten because the tenant subdomain is the employer.

ats_note: A requisition id is only ever an identity together with its ATS system and tenant. requisition_id 12345 on two unrelated ATS systems is two different jobs, and this artifact provides no key under which they could collide.

company.legal_suffix_note: Stripped repeatedly from the end only, and never to an empty string. Nothing else is removed: a country or division qualifier such as 'Group - India' is retained, because dropping it would merge a subsidiary into its parent.
never: stopword removal beyond the declared legal suffixes

title.note: Two titles match only when they normalize to the same string. 'AI QA Engineer' and 'AI Quality Assurance Engineer' are different titles here, and that is the intended conservative reading.

never: treating an absent location as a wildcard
location.unknown_tokens_note: A location normalizing to one of these is NOT EVALUABLE, exactly as an absent location is. It is never positive identity evidence and never matches another unknown.

near_match_rules.condition: normalized_company and normalized_title are equal, and normalized_location is not evaluable on at least one side.
near_match_rules.note: P0_SPEC 8.3: a near-match rather than an exact match does not assert identity. An absent location is not evidence of sameness.

distinctness_rules.condition: normalized_company and normalized_title are equal, both locations are evaluable, and they differ.
distinctness_rules.note: Two requisitions for the same title at the same employer in different locations are different requisitions. A differing evaluable location is counter-evidence, not a near-match.

conflict_rules.condition: Both records carry an L1 key for the same source_portal and the external_ids differ.

Both records carry a canonical identity URL that was REBUILT FROM a source-native id (a host family declaring canonical_path_template), they are in the same host family, and the canonical URLs differ.
conflict_rules.note: Restricted to id-derived canonical URLs on purpose. Two URLs on one ATS host that differ only by locale prefix or title slug are the same requisition, not a contradiction, and one posting legitimately has both a LinkedIn URL and an employer ATS URL.

conflict_rules.condition: Both records carry an ATS requisition for the same (ats_system, ats_tenant) and the requisition_ids differ.

conflict_note: A conflict downgrades a suppression-grade match to IDENTITY_UNCERTAIN. It never upgrades anything. Differing L3 text alongside an L1/L2/L4 match is recorded as a noted difference, not a conflict: employers rename and postings get re-titled, and a title edit is not evidence of a different job.

match_scope.opportunities_note: P0_SPEC 8.4: matching an opportunities row is what prevents re-surfacing something already applied to. Every status is in scope, including applied, rejected and archived rows.
match_scope.opportunities_l1_derivation: opportunities has no external_id column. An L1 key is derived for an opportunities row ONLY when its job_url matches a declared host family whose posting path contains the source-native id. That is reading an id the URL demonstrably carries, not inferring one.
match_scope.read_only_note: The resolver opens the database read-only. Identity is not application outcome: no status, stage, verdict, score or human decision is read as input or written as output.

determinism.candidate_ordering: Index records are compared in ascending record_ref order.
determinism.best_match_selection: Highest-confidence matching layer first, in declared layer order L1, L2, L4, L3; ties broken by ascending record_ref.
determinism.note: The same candidate against the same index yields a byte-identical resolution record modulo resolved_at.

ID-L1-MATCH.meaning: Same source portal and same source-native external id.

ID-L3-MATCH.meaning: Same normalized company, title and location.

ID-L4-MATCH.meaning: Same ATS system, tenant and requisition id.

ID-L3-PARTIAL.meaning: Company and title match; location is not evaluable on at least one side. Identity is not asserted.

ID-L3-LOCATION-DIFFERS.meaning: Company and title match but both locations are evaluable and differ. Treated as distinct.

ID-NO-MATCH.meaning: No identity layer matched any record in scope.

ID-L1-ABSENT.meaning: No source-native external id is available for this record.

ID-L4-ABSENT.meaning: No ATS requisition id is available for this record.

ID-L3-NOT-EVALUABLE.meaning: Company, title or location is missing, so L3 was not evaluated.

ID-URL-ABSENT.meaning: No URL was supplied for this record.

ID-URL-UNSUPPORTED-SCHEME.meaning: URL scheme is not http or https. Not usable as an identity.

ID-URL-UNPARSEABLE.meaning: URL could not be parsed into a host and path.

ID-URL-ROOT-ONLY.meaning: URL addresses a host root with no posting path. Not a posting.

ID-URL-FRAGMENT-ONLY.meaning: URL distinguished only by a fragment. P0_SPEC 8.2 states such a URL is not a posting.

ID-URL-LISTING-PAGE.meaning: URL addresses a listing or company board, not a single posting.

ID-URL-NOT-A-POSTING-PATH.meaning: Host belongs to a declared family and the path does not match that family's posting form.

ID-CONFLICT-L1.meaning: Same portal, different source-native external ids.

ID-CONFLICT-L2.meaning: Same host family, different canonical identity URLs.

ID-CONFLICT-L4.meaning: Same ATS system and tenant, different requisition ids.

prohibited: Auto-merging on fuzzy or near-match evidence (P0_SPEC 8.3).
Treating an absent or UNKNOWN value as positive identity evidence.
Collapsing IDENTITY_UNCERTAIN into a duplicate outcome.
Deleting, merging or rewriting any existing row. The resolver detects, classifies and reports.
Reading or writing application status, stage, gate verdict or score.
Re-evaluating eligibility. Identity is not a policy layer.
